rawInput.answer: In compose.ts's dispatch(i), each middleware call is individually try/caught: `await handler(context, () => dispatch(i+1))`. Because next() (dispatch(i+1)) executes inside that awaited call, an error surfaces at the innermost active dispatch frame first — if `onError` was supplied to compose() and the thrown value is an Error, it's converted to a Response there and dispatch returns normally (so outer middleware's own try/catch around next() never sees it, only context.error/context.res); otherwise it's rethrown and bubbles to whatever caller does have an onError (or none, in which case it keeps propagating). report.answer: In compose.ts's dispatch(i), each middleware call is individually try/caught: `await handler(context, () => dispatch(i+1))`. Because next() (dispatch(i+1)) executes inside that awaited call, an error surfaces at the innermost active dispatch frame first — if `onError` was supplied to compose() and the thrown value is an Error, it's converted to a Response there and dispatch returns normally (so outer middleware's own try/catch around next() never sees it, only context.error/context.res); otherwise it's rethrown and bubbles to whatever caller does have an onError (or none, in which case it keeps propagating). Hono's #dispatch() supplies `this.errorHandler` (default: unwrap HTTPException via getResponse(), else log + 500; overridable via app.onError()) as compose's onError for the main route stack, and wraps the whole composed(c) call plus the single-handler fast path in its own try/catch as a final safety net for non-Error throws and the "context not finalized" check.
